insider_note: The middle step — evaluating ∫₀^π dx/(1+sinx) by multiplying top and bottom by (1−sinx) — is a standalone trick worth memorising on its own; it turns up whenever 1+sinx or 1−sinx sits alone in a denominator.

steps.label: Apply the King's property
steps.margin_note: First two marks. sin(π − x) stays sinx, so only the x out front changes.
steps.memory_tip: sin(π − x) = sinx always — the denominator here never changes under this substitution.
lines: I = ∫₀^π (π − x)sin(π − x)/(1 + sin(π − x)) dx
steps.why: sin(π − x) = sinx, so the denominator 1 + sinx is unchanged by the substitution — only the x in the numerator becomes π − x, setting up the cancellation in the next step.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to replace BOTH the x in front and the sinx inside the denominator's argument.

steps.label: Add and split into two integrals
steps.margin_note: Two more marks. The 1/(1+sinx) split is the setup for the next step's trick.
steps.memory_tip: 1/(1+sinx) always splits into 1 minus 1/(1+sinx) — write it as [1 + sinx − 1]/(1 + sinx).
steps.why: Writing sinx as (1 + sinx) − 1 splits the fraction into a constant 1 and a leftover 1/(1+sinx) term, turning the integral into two easy pieces: a plain x-integral and one that needs a separate trick.
common_mistakes: Trying to integrate sinx/(1+sinx) directly without the split.
Losing the overall factor of π when distributing it across the two new integrals.

steps.label: Evaluate ∫dx/(1 + sinx)
steps.margin_note: Two marks for this standalone sub-integral.
steps.memory_tip: Multiply top and bottom by (1 − sinx) whenever 1 + sinx sits alone in a denominator — it turns cos²x up top.
steps.why: Multiplying by (1 − sinx)/(1 − sinx) clears the sinx from the denominator using 1 − sin²x = cos²x, leaving a sum of two standard antiderivatives — tanx and secx — that can be evaluated directly.
common_mistakes: Losing the negative sign when distributing (1 − sinx)/cos²x into sec²x − secx tanx.

steps.label: Combine for the final answer
steps.margin_note: The last mark. Substitute the value 2 from step 3 back into equation (3).
steps.memory_tip: π² minus π times 2 gives π² − 2π — halve it for I.
steps.why: Substituting the value 2, found in the previous step, back into 2I = π² − π∫dx/(1+sinx) and dividing by 2 gives the final answer directly.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to divide the whole expression by 2 at the end.
Writing the answer as (π² − 2π)/2 without simplifying to π²/2 − π.
